title: Playlist Validation & Efficiency
description: Implements all improvements from the flutter-playlist-pilot-analysis.md report. Four layers: runtime efficiency (R1-R3), playlist runtime (R4-R9), gate system (§2.11), playlist authoring (§2.12), and observability (R10-R14). 17 child tasks covering cross-bead context, project file pre-inclusion, playlist reload, gate scripts, playlist init/create subcommands, cost tracking, and more.

title: Cross-bead context handoff
description:
Report ref: R1. Estimated savings: $15-20/run (150-200 turns).

When a bead task closes, capture a ~200-word summary of what changed and inject it into the next bead's prompt as a ## Prior Task Context section. This eliminates the 5-10 turn "explore the codebase" phase at the start of every task.

Implementation:
* In lib/task_outcome.sh handle_task_outcome(), after a task closes (status=closed), extract the last assistant text block from the stream-json log file ($INVOKE_LOG). Store it in a global LAST_TASK_SUMMARY.
* Extraction: use jq to find the last assistant message with type=text from the JSONL, truncate to ~200 words.
* In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), if LAST_TASK_SUMMARY is non-empty, append a section after ## Your Task:
  ## Prior Task Context
  The previous task in this session produced the following summary:
  $LAST_TASK_SUMMARY
* Also include LAST_TASK_SUMMARY in build_raw_prompt() for prompt-type playlist lines.
* Clear LAST_TASK_SUMMARY after injecting it (so it doesn't repeat if the same task retries).

Acceptance criteria:
* After a bead closes, LAST_TASK_SUMMARY contains a meaningful excerpt from the stream log
* The next invocation's prompt includes ## Prior Task Context with that excerpt
* Summary is cleared after use
* If no prior task (first task in session), section is omitted

title: Gate template expansion in playlist authoring
description:
Report ref: §2.11. Depends on: ralph-0h1.9 (gate template system).

Integrates the gate template system into the playlist authoring pipeline. When ralph playlist init or ralph playlist create runs, this inserts #TAG shorthand lines at appropriate intervals. The tags are NOT expanded here — they stay as shorthand in the file and get expanded at runtime (task 9).

Implementation:
* In lib/gates.sh, add playlist_inject_gates():
  * Takes a playlist file path as input
  * Reads the file line by line, tracking:
    * Bead count since last gate
    * Current epic (parent of current bead, via br show)
    * Whether a #SMOKE_TEST has appeared yet
  * Insertion rules:
    * Every ~5 beads without a gate: insert "> #COMPLETENESS_SCAN" line
    * At epic boundaries (parent epic changes): insert ">@opus #REVIEW" line
    * After first 5 beads if no #SMOKE_TEST exists: insert ">@opus #SMOKE_TEST" line
  * Inserted lines are shorthand tags only — no expansion. Example insertions:
    > #COMPLETENESS_SCAN
    >@opus #SMOKE_TEST
    >@opus #REVIEW
  * The user can add context to these lines later, or Claude can during semantic validation (task 13)
  * Write the augmented playlist back to the file
  * Return count of gates injected

* This function is called by:
  * playlist_validate_semantic() (task 13) — injects missing gates during init, then Claude refines them with context
  * playlist_create() (task 14) — injects gates as post-creation pass

* The self-healing aspect (review prompt discovers issues, creates beads, injects into playlist) is handled by the expanded prompt instructions at runtime plus playlist reload (task 4).

Acceptance criteria:
* playlist_inject_gates() inserts #TAG shorthand lines at correct intervals
* Completeness scans every ~5 beads without a gate
* Review prompts at epic boundaries
* Smoke test after first 5 beads if missing
* Tags are shorthand only — NOT expanded in the file
* Function is reusable by both init and create flows
* Returns count of injected gates

title: Validation marker check on playlist startup
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path A. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (syntax validation).

When ralph --playlist FILE is invoked, check for a validation marker. If absent, warn and offer options. The fallback only offers Phase 1 (syntax validation) until Phase 2 (semantic, task 13) is implemented — this avoids a broken code path.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_init(), after loading the file into PLAYLIST_LINES:
  * Scan first 5 lines for a line matching: # ✓ VALIDATED:
  * If found: log "Playlist validated: <marker line>" and continue
  * If not found and not DRY_RUN:
    * Print warning:
      [ralph] WARNING: Playlist not validated.
        Missing: quality gates, API verification, completeness scan
        Run 'ralph playlist init $PLAYLIST' to validate and add quality gates.
        Continue anyway? [y/N]
    * Read user input:
      * y or Y: continue (log "Proceeding without validation")
      * n or N or empty:
        * Check if playlist_validate_semantic function exists (Phase 2 implemented):
          * If yes: offer full init: "Run 'ralph playlist init $PLAYLIST' now? [Y/n]"
            * Y: run playlist_validate_syntax then playlist_validate_semantic, reload, continue
            * n: exit 1
          * If no (Phase 2 not yet implemented): offer syntax-only:
            "Run syntax validation on $PLAYLIST? [Y/n]"
            * Y: run playlist_validate_syntax only, continue (no marker added — that's Phase 2's job)
            * n: exit 1
    * Non-interactive (no TTY): skip prompt, log warning, continue.
  * If DRY_RUN: log warning, don't prompt.

Acceptance criteria:
* Playlist with "# ✓ VALIDATED:" in first 5 lines proceeds without warning
* Playlist without marker shows warning and prompts
* y continues without validation
* n offers inline init (full if Phase 2 exists, syntax-only otherwise)
* Non-interactive skips prompt with warning
* Dry-run logs warning only
* No broken code path if Phase 2 (task 13) isn't implemented yet

title: ralph playlist init — syntax validation phase
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path C, Phase 1. This is the deterministic phase of ralph playlist init.

Add a ralph playlist init <file> subcommand. Phase 1 validates syntax AND gate density deterministically — no Claude invocation. Phase 2 (task 13, semantic validation via Claude) runs automatically if Phase 1 passes.

Implementation:
* In lib/args.sh parse_args(), detect "playlist" as first arg followed by "init":
  * ralph playlist init <file> — set PLAYLIST_INIT_MODE=true, PLAYLIST=<file>
  * After parse_args, if PLAYLIST_INIT_MODE, call playlist_validate_syntax. If it passes, call playlist_validate_semantic (task 13). Then exit.

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_validate_syntax():
  Two sub-phases, both deterministic:

  **Phase 1a: Line-by-line syntax**
  * Read the playlist file line by line
  * For each non-blank, non-comment line:
    * If starts with ">": valid prompt line, no further check needed
    * Otherwise: treat as bead ID. Run br show "$line" --json 2>/dev/null
      * If br show fails (exit non-zero): ERROR — "$line" is not a valid bead ID or prompt
      * If br show succeeds but status is "closed" or "done": WARNING — bead "$line" is already closed
  * Track error_count and warning_count

  **Phase 1b: Gate density analysis**
  * Call gate_check_playlist() from lib/gates.sh (task 9) to analyze gate presence
  * Call gate_minimum_rules() to enforce requirements:
    * Zero gates in a playlist with >1 bead = ERROR (blocks)
    * Low density (fewer than 1 gate per 7 beads) = WARNING
    * Missing #COMPLETENESS_SCAN (none per 10 beads or per epic) = WARNING
    * Missing #SMOKE_TEST (none and playlist has >5 beads) = WARNING
    * Missing #REVIEW (none at epic boundaries) = WARNING
  * Gate errors are added to error_count, gate warnings to warning_count

  **Report:**
  [ralph] Syntax validation:
    Line 15: ERROR — "chippie ogz3.1" is not a valid bead ID or prompt
    Line 41: WARNING — bead "chippie-xyz.99" does not exist in beads

  Gate analysis:
    Beads: 39  |  Gates: 0  |  Density: 0:39
    ERROR: No quality gates found. Every playlist needs at least 1 gate.
    WARNING: No #SMOKE_TEST found. Recommend API validation after foundation beads.
    WARNING: No #COMPLETENESS_SCAN found. Recommend TODO/FIXME scan every 10 beads.

    3 errors, 2 warnings. Fix errors before proceeding.

  * Exit 1 if errors > 0. Exit 0 if only warnings or clean.
  * If exit 0: Phase 2 (task 13) runs automatically — Claude adds missing gates, verifies endpoints, adds validation marker.

Acceptance criteria:
* ralph playlist init foo.playlist validates line syntax AND gate density
* Invalid bead IDs and zero gates are errors (block Phase 2)
* Low density and missing gate types are warnings (don't block)
* Gate analysis uses gate_check_playlist() and gate_minimum_rules() from task 9
* Phase 2 (semantic, task 13) runs automatically on Phase 1 success
* From user perspective: one command does both phases
* Exit code 1 on errors, 0 on clean/warnings-only

title: ralph playlist init — semantic validation phase
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path C, Phase 2. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (syntax validation), ralph-0h1.10 (gate template expansion).

Phase 2 of ralph playlist init. Runs automatically after Phase 1 (syntax + gate density) passes. First injects missing gate #TAG shorthand lines deterministically, then invokes Claude to add context to those tags and audit bead descriptions.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_validate_semantic(). Called automatically by Phase 1 on success.

  **Step 1: Deterministic gate injection**
  * Call playlist_inject_gates() from lib/gates.sh (task 10) to insert missing #TAG shorthand lines at appropriate intervals.
  * Log how many gates were injected. E.g. "Injected 3 gates: 1 #SMOKE_TEST, 1 #REVIEW, 1 #COMPLETENESS_SCAN"

  **Step 2: Claude semantic audit**
  * Gather context:
    * Playlist file contents (now including injected #TAG lines from step 1)
    * For each bead ID: br show <id> --json (title + description)
    * Project .ralph/config contents (if exists)
    * List of key files in the project
  * Build a prompt for Claude with instructions:
    You are validating a ralph playlist file. #TAG shorthand lines have been auto-inserted.
    Audit and improve:
    1. Add context to bare #TAG lines. For example, change:
         >@opus #SMOKE_TEST
       to:
         >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl POST /api/v1/auth/login, verify token, test GET /clients with token
       The context should be specific to what was implemented in the surrounding beads.
    2. Verify each bead description against the real codebase:
       * curl every API endpoint referenced (if backend is running)
       * Check that file paths in descriptions exist
       * Flag fabricated URLs or nonexistent endpoints
       * Update bead descriptions via br update where wrong
    3. Check for missing backend dependencies — create backend beads if needed
    4. Add validation marker: # ✓ VALIDATED: <timestamp> by ralph playlist init
    5. Print a report of every change made
  * Call invoke_claude with this prompt
  * Log: "Playlist validation complete. Review changes with: git diff $PLAYLIST"

Acceptance criteria:
* Phase 2 runs automatically after Phase 1 passes
* playlist_inject_gates() (task 10) inserts bare #TAG shorthand lines first
* Claude adds project-specific context to the bare tags
* Claude can verify endpoints, update bead descriptions, create backend beads
* Validation marker is added to line 1
* Changes are visible via git diff
* If Claude invocation fails, log warning and exit (don't corrupt the file)

title: ralph playlist create from beads/epics
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path B. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (reuses syntax validation), ralph-0h1.10 (gate injection).

Add ralph playlist create subcommand that generates a playlist from bead IDs or epics. Two-pass: Claude generates the bead ordering and initial #TAG placements, then playlist_inject_gates() (task 10) ensures minimum gate density by inserting any missing #TAG shorthand lines.

Implementation:
* In lib/args.sh parse_args(), detect "playlist" as first arg followed by "create":
  * ralph playlist create <id1> <id2> ... -o <output-file>
  * ralph playlist create --epic <epic-id> -o <output-file>
  * ralph playlist create --epic <id1> --epic <id2> -o <output-file>
  * Set PLAYLIST_CREATE_MODE=true, collect bead IDs or epic IDs, set OUTPUT_FILE

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_create():

  **Step 1: Gather bead details**
  * If --epic flags: expand to children via br ready --parent=<id> -r --json in dependency order.
  * If raw bead IDs: use as-is.
  * For each bead: br show <id> --json for title + description.

  **Step 2: Claude generates playlist**
  * Build creation prompt with mandatory rules:
    * Order beads by dependency
    * VERIFY EVERY API ENDPOINT referenced in bead descriptions
    * FLAG FABRICATED INFORMATION
    * TRACK BACKEND DEPENDENCIES — create backend beads if needed
    * Include #TAG gate lines with context at appropriate intervals:
      * #COMPLETENESS_SCAN every ~5 beads
      * #SMOKE_TEST after auth/foundation
      * #REVIEW at epic boundaries
    * Add context to each #TAG based on surrounding beads
    * MARK AS VALIDATED with timestamp
    * Write to $OUTPUT_FILE
  * Call invoke_claude

  **Step 3: Ensure gate density**
  * Call playlist_inject_gates() (task 10) on generated file
  * Fills any gaps Claude missed with bare #TAG lines
  * Log adjustments

  **Step 4: Syntax validation sanity check**
  * Run playlist_validate_syntax() (task 12)
  * Catches malformed bead IDs or density violations
  * Log: "Playlist created: $OUTPUT_FILE (N beads, M gates, P prompts)"

Acceptance criteria:
* ralph playlist create <ids> -o out.playlist generates a valid playlist file
* ralph playlist create --epic <id> expands epic children in dependency order
* Multiple --epic flags combine children
* Claude places #TAG lines with context
* playlist_inject_gates() ensures minimum density as a safety net
* playlist_validate_syntax() confirms correctness
* Output reports bead count, gate count, prompt count

title: Cost tracking in state
description:
Report ref: R10.

Track cumulative cost across the session. Parse cost from each stream-json log's result entry and maintain a running total in .ralph_state.

Implementation:
* In lib/config.sh or lib/utils.sh, add global: total_cost_usd="0.00"
* In lib/utils.sh save_state(), persist total_cost_usd to .ralph_state
* In lib/utils.sh load_state(), restore total_cost_usd from .ralph_state
* In lib/invoke.sh _invoke_claude_once(), after successful invocation:
  * Parse the result entry from $INVOKE_LOG:
    cost=$(tail -5 "$INVOKE_LOG" | jq -r 'select(.type=="result") | .cost_usd // 0' 2>/dev/null)
  * Note: the stream-json result event may have cost in different fields depending on Claude CLI version. Check for .cost_usd, .total_cost, or compute from .usage if needed. Use awk for floating-point addition:
    total_cost_usd=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $total_cost_usd + ${cost:-0}}")
* In lib/lifecycle.sh cleanup(), add cost to the summary box:
  printf '│  Total cost:      $%-8s\n' "$total_cost_usd"
* In lib/monitor.sh (if feasible), show running cost in the dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
* total_cost_usd accumulates across invocations within a session
* Value persists in .ralph_state (survives crash + resume)
* Cleanup summary shows total cost
* Cost parsing handles missing/malformed result entries gracefully (defaults to 0)

title: Playlist progress file
description:
Report ref: R14.

Write .ralph/playlist-progress.md after each task completes. Human-readable status of what's done, what's next, what's blocked. Useful for monitoring without the TUI dashboard.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_write_progress():
  * Write to .ralph/playlist-progress.md
  * Format:
    # Playlist Progress: <playlist filename>
    Updated: <timestamp>
    ## Status: <completed>/<total> items (N beads, M prompts)
    ## Completed
    * [bead] chippie-ogz3.1 — Title (closed)
    * [prompt] Review changes (@opus)
    ## Next Up
    * [bead] chippie-hweb.1 — Title (ready)
    ## Remaining
    * [bead] chippie-hweb.2 — Title
    * ...
  * Iterate PLAYLIST_LINES, classify each as completed (before playlist_line), next (at playlist_line), or remaining (after).
  * For bead lines, include title from br show --json (cache to avoid repeated lookups).
* Call playlist_write_progress() from save_state() when in playlist mode (after playlist_advance).

Acceptance criteria:
* .ralph/playlist-progress.md is updated after each task completes
* Shows completed, next, and remaining sections
* Includes bead titles and statuses
* Timestamp is current
* File is human-readable in any editor

title: Pre-computed project summary at session start
description:
Report ref: R12.

Generate .ralph/project-context.md at session start via a quick Claude invocation. Contains directory structure, key files, dependency versions, architecture patterns. All subsequent tasks can reference this instead of re-exploring.

Implementation:
* In lib/lifecycle.sh initialize(), after init_invoke and playlist_init:
  * Check if .ralph/project-context.md needs regeneration:
    * Does not exist → regenerate
    * File exists but is older than 24 hours → regenerate
    * File exists and N+ commits have been made since generation (store the HEAD commit hash in the first line as a comment: <!-- generated-at: abc123 -->. Compare current HEAD to stored hash. If >10 commits differ, regenerate) → regenerate
    * Otherwise → use cached ("Using cached project summary")
  * To regenerate:
    * Build a short prompt:
      Analyze this project and write a concise project summary to .ralph/project-context.md.
      Include: directory structure (tree -L 2), key files and their purposes, dependency versions
      (from package.json/pubspec.yaml/requirements.txt/Cargo.toml), architecture patterns observed,
      and any conventions (naming, testing, etc). Keep it under 300 lines.
      Add <!-- generated-at: COMMIT_HASH --> as the first line.
      Output ONLY the file — no commentary.
    * Set MODEL to "haiku" for this (cheapest model, simple task)
    * Call invoke_claude with this prompt
    * Log: "Project summary generated: .ralph/project-context.md"
  * If file exists and is fresh, log: "Using cached project summary"
* In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), if .ralph/project-context.md exists:
  * Read and include under ## Project Summary (truncated to 100 lines)
  * This is complementary to CONTEXT_FILES (task 2) — summary is high-level overview, context file map is specific navigation.
* User can delete .ralph/project-context.md to force regeneration on next run.

Acceptance criteria:
* First run generates .ralph/project-context.md via Claude (haiku)
* Subsequent runs reuse if file is <24h old AND <10 commits since generation
* Stale file (>24h or >10 commits) is regenerated
* Deleting the file forces regeneration
* Summary is included in prompts when available
* If generation fails, log warning and continue without summary

title: Pre-include project context files in prompt
description:
Report ref: R2. Estimated savings: $22/run (290 Read calls eliminated).

Add a CONTEXT_FILES config variable that generates a file manifest included in every prompt. Instead of dumping entire file contents (which would bloat prompts), include a structured map: path, purpose, and key exports/patterns. This tells Claude WHERE things are without making it discover them each time.

Implementation:
* In lib/config.sh, add: CONTEXT_FILES="" (empty default, set per-project in .ralph/config)
* In .ralph/config template (lib/lifecycle.sh init_project()), add commented example:
  # CONTEXT_FILES="pubspec.yaml,lib/main.dart,lib/core/routing/app_router.dart"
* In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), after the ## Rules section, if CONTEXT_FILES is non-empty:
  * Split on comma, iterate each path
  * For each file that exists, include a brief manifest entry:
    ## Project File Map
    * pubspec.yaml — project dependencies and configuration
    * lib/main.dart — app entry point, provider setup, router init
    * lib/core/routing/app_router.dart — GoRouter route definitions
  * Generate the purpose line by reading the first docstring/comment block (first 5 lines) from each file
  * Do NOT include full file contents — just path + purpose
* Also include in build_raw_prompt() for prompt-type lines.
* Add --context-files CLI flag in lib/args.sh that overrides CONTEXT_FILES.
* This pairs with task 17 (project summary) — the summary gives architecture overview, the file map gives specific navigation pointers.

Acceptance criteria:
* Setting CONTEXT_FILES in .ralph/config includes a file map in every prompt
* Map shows path + purpose, NOT full contents
* --context-files flag works and overrides config
* Missing files are silently skipped with a log warning
* init_project() template includes commented CONTEXT_FILES example
* Prompt size increase is minimal (a few lines per file, not hundreds)

title: Add no-agent-spawning rule to prompt
description:
Report ref: R3. Estimated savings: $7.50/run.

80% of tasks in the pilot spawned Explore agents that were 6x slower and more expensive than direct file reads. Add a prompt rule encouraging direct tool use over agent spawning, while allowing agents for genuinely exploratory work.

Implementation:
* In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), add rule 7 (after existing rule 6):
  7. Prefer Read, Grep, and Glob tools for file operations. Only spawn Agent sub-tasks when exploring unfamiliar parts of the codebase that are not described in this task or the project context. Direct tool use is faster and cheaper.
* Also add this rule to build_raw_prompt() as rule 6.

Acceptance criteria:
* Both build_prompt() and build_raw_prompt() include the agent guidance rule
* Rule discourages unnecessary agent spawning without banning it outright
* Rule numbering is sequential and correct

title: Playlist reload after prompt execution
description:
Report ref: R6. Enables dynamic playlist injection (§2.10).

After a > prompt completes, reload the playlist file in case the prompt injected new lines. Ralph reads PLAYLIST_LINES from a cached array; if a prompt modifies the file, new lines are invisible until reloaded.

## Safety Invariants

1. Ralph reads the playlist file ONLY after invoke_claude returns. Never during. Since invoke_claude is synchronous (ralph waits), there is no concurrent read/write. Future contributors: do NOT add async reads of the playlist file.

2. Before any reload that detects changes, back up the current playlist:
   cp "$PLAYLIST" ".ralph/playlist-backup-$(date +%s)"
   This is cheap insurance against injection that makes things worse.

3. Line position tracking: playlist_line is a line number. After injection, lines shift. The reload function must handle this correctly:
   * Store the content of the current line before reload (content hash or literal string).
   * After re-reading the file, verify the line at playlist_line still matches.
   * If it doesn't (lines were inserted ABOVE current position — unusual but possible from a user edit), scan forward to find the matching line and adjust playlist_line.
   * Normal case: injections happen AFTER current position, so playlist_line stays valid.

## Implementation

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_reload():
  * Back up playlist file if content has changed (compare line count or checksum)
  * Re-read the playlist file into PLAYLIST_LINES (same logic as playlist_init)
  * Verify current line position still matches expected content
  * If mismatch: scan for the correct line, adjust playlist_line, log warning
  * Recount playlist_total
  * Log if line count changed: "Playlist reloaded: N new lines detected (backup: .ralph/playlist-backup-TIMESTAMP)"
  * If unchanged: no log, no backup (silent no-op)

* In playlist_execute_prompt(), call playlist_reload after invoke_claude returns successfully.
* Do NOT reload after bead execution (beads don't modify the playlist file).

Acceptance criteria:
* If a prompt invocation adds lines after current position, they are picked up on next playlist_next()
* If the file is unchanged, reload is a silent no-op
* Playlist is backed up before reload when changes detected
* Line position is verified by content match, not just line number
* If position mismatch: ralph scans and adjusts (does not skip beads)
* playlist_total is recounted
* Ralph never reads the playlist during a Claude invocation

title: Handle bead status done as closed
description:
Report ref: R9.

Ralph got a WARNING for bead status "done" during the pilot (chippie-7m1j.1). The "done" status should be treated as equivalent to "closed" in all ralph logic.

Implementation:
* In lib/invoke.sh check_bead_status(), map "done" to "closed":
  After getting bead_status from jq, add:
  [[ "$bead_status" == "done" ]] && bead_status="closed"
* In lib/playlist.sh bead_already_closed() (used in playlist_execute to skip closed beads):
  Check for both "closed" and "done" status values.
  Currently checks: status == "closed". Change to: status == "closed" or status == "done".
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_dry_run(), same mapping for the status display.

Acceptance criteria:
* A bead with status "done" is treated as closed in task_outcome flow
* A bead with status "done" is skipped in playlist mode (same as closed)
* Dry-run shows "done" beads as "already closed"
* No WARNING logged for "done" status
close_reason: DROPPED: 'done' status is a beads_rust issue, not a ralph issue. If 'done' is not a legitimate br status, the fix belongs in br (reject or alias it). Ralph should not paper over improper tool usage. Filed as br concern instead.

title: Dry-run validation warnings for missing gates
description:
Report ref: R5. Depends on: ralph-0h1.9 (gate template system) for gate_check_playlist().

ralph --playlist FILE --dry-run should report gate density analysis alongside the existing bead validation. Uses gate_check_playlist() from lib/gates.sh instead of ad-hoc string matching.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_dry_run_summary(), after the existing per-bead warnings:
  * Call gate_check_playlist() to get the full density report
  * Print a GATE ANALYSIS section:
    GATE ANALYSIS:
      Beads: 39  |  Gates: 4  |  Density: 1:10 (recommend 1:7)
      #SMOKE_TEST: 1  |  #COMPLETENESS_SCAN: 1  |  #REVIEW: 2
  * If gate_minimum_rules() returns errors (zero gates): print as ERROR
  * If gate_minimum_rules() returns warnings (low density, missing types): print as RECOMMENDATIONS:
    RECOMMENDATIONS:
      * Low gate density (1:10). Recommend at least 1 gate per 7 beads.
      * No #SMOKE_TEST detected. Recommend adding API validation after foundation beads.
      * Recommend running 'ralph playlist init' to add quality gates.
  * Non-blocking (dry-run still completes regardless of gate analysis)

Acceptance criteria:
* Dry-run shows gate density analysis (bead count, gate count, ratio)
* Dry-run shows per-template type counts
* Zero gates shows as ERROR level
* Low density or missing types show as RECOMMENDATIONS
* Uses gate_check_playlist() from task 9, not ad-hoc string matching
* Non-blocking (dry-run always completes)

title: Loop counter visibility improvements
description:
Report ref: R8.

The current loop display is dim and easy to miss. Replace with a bold separator line showing loop number, task ID, and model. Include blank lines before and after for visual breathing room.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_execute_bead(), add a prominent header before claim_task:
  log ""
  log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  log "  LOOP $((total_loops + 1))/$MAX_LOOPS  │  Task: $tid  │  Model: $MODEL"
  log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  log ""
* Update the existing header in playlist_execute_prompt() to match the same format:
  log ""
  log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  log "  LOOP $((total_loops + 1))/$MAX_LOOPS  │  Prompt  │  Model: $MODEL"
  log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  log ""
* Also update the standard mode loop header in the main ralph script to use the same format.
* Newlines before AND after the box for visual separation.

Acceptance criteria:
* All loop iterations (bead, prompt, standard mode) show the bold separator format
* Blank lines before and after the box
* Task ID or "Prompt" is shown as appropriate
* Model is visible in the header

title: Per-line annotation framework (@turns, @timeout, @model)
description:
Report ref: R7 + R13. Generalizes the existing @model override to a full annotation system.

Support inline metadata on playlist lines: chippie-ogz3.1 @turns=30 @timeout=10 @model=haiku
Parsed by playlist_next(), forwarded to invocation.

Turn/timeout behavior on retry: annotations set the budget for the FIRST attempt only. If the task fails and retries, fall back to global MAX_TURNS/TIMEOUT_MINUTES. The annotation is "try to finish in N turns" — if it can't, the retry gets the full budget to finish the job. This prevents the failure loop where a task that needs 25 turns keeps failing at 20 and exhausts retries.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_next(), after classifying bead vs prompt:
  * For bead lines: extract annotations from after the bead ID. Split on whitespace, look for @key=value patterns.
  * For prompt lines: @model is already parsed (without =). Extend to also support @turns=N and @timeout=M. Keep backward compat with >@opus (no =).
  * Set globals: playlist_line_model (existing), playlist_line_turns (new), playlist_line_timeout (new).
  * Default all to empty string (meaning "use global default").
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_execute_bead() and playlist_execute_prompt():
  * If playlist_line_turns is non-empty, save MAX_TURNS, override, restore after invoke_claude.
  * If playlist_line_timeout is non-empty, save TIMEOUT_MINUTES, override, recalc TIMEOUT_SECS, restore after invoke_claude.
  * On retry (task still in_progress, re-invoked): clear the annotation overrides and use global values. The annotation only applies to the first attempt.
  * playlist_line_model already handled in playlist_execute_prompt(). Extend same pattern to playlist_execute_bead().
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_dry_run(), display annotations if present:
  log "  1. [bead] chippie-ogz3.1 — Title (@turns=30, @timeout=10)"
* Update the loop counter header (task 7) to show overrides if active.

Acceptance criteria:
* @turns=30 on a bead line sets MAX_TURNS=30 for that invocation only
* @timeout=15 sets TIMEOUT_MINUTES=15 for that invocation only
* @model=opus sets MODEL=opus for that invocation only (beads and prompts)
* All three can be combined: chippie-xxx @turns=30 @timeout=15 @model=sonnet
* On retry: annotation limits are cleared, global values used instead
* Global values are restored after each invocation (whether success or retry)
* Dry-run shows annotations
* Backward compat: >@opus still works (no = sign)

title: Quality gate template system
description:
Report ref: §2.11, reworked based on review + external review feedback.

Quality gates are > prompt lines with template tags like #SMOKE_TEST, #COMPLETENESS_SCAN, #REVIEW. Tags are resolved at RUNTIME when ralph builds the prompt for Claude — same mechanism as @opus resolves the model. The playlist file is never modified by expansion.

## Tag Syntax Rules

* One tag per line. Multiple tags on a single line (e.g. > #SMOKE_TEST #REVIEW) is a parse ERROR.
* Unknown tags (not in GATE_TEMPLATES) are a hard ERROR at parse time in playlist_next(). Ralph halts with: "Unknown gate template: #NONEXISTENT on line N. Valid tags: #SMOKE_TEST, #COMPLETENESS_SCAN, #REVIEW"
* Tag-only lines with no user context are valid: > #COMPLETENESS_SCAN expands to just the template base text.
* Tag + user context: >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl the auth endpoints — template text + user context appended.

## Runtime Expansion (in playlist_execute_prompt)

Playlist line: >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl every flutter api endpoint against localhost:8080

Ralph parses in playlist_next():
  @opus           → sets playlist_line_model="opus"
  #SMOKE_TEST     → sets playlist_line_gate_tag="SMOKE_TEST"
  "curl every..." → sets playlist_line_gate_context="curl every..."

In playlist_execute_prompt(), before build_raw_prompt():
  If playlist_line_gate_tag is set, call gate_expand_tag(tag, context).
  Returns: template base text + "\n" + user context.
  Pass expanded text to build_raw_prompt(). The #TAG never reaches Claude.

## Implementation

* Create lib/gates.sh with:

  1. GATE_TEMPLATES associative array — base prompt text per tag:
     * SMOKE_TEST: "Test API endpoints against live backend. curl each endpoint implemented in the last batch of beads. Verify responses match expected schemas. If issues found: create beads (type=bug only) with br create, insert IDs into the playlist file after this line."
     * COMPLETENESS_SCAN: "Scan for incomplete work: grep -rn 'TODO|FIXME|HACK|STUB|placeholder|not yet|not implemented' in the project source. For each match in code written during this playlist, implement it fully or remove it with justification. If issues require separate tasks: create beads (type=bug only) and inject into playlist."
     * REVIEW: "Review the work completed in the last epic. Check architecture, patterns, test coverage. Flag issues. If significant work needed: create beads (type=bug only) and inject into playlist."

  2. gate_expand_tag(tag, context): looks up GATE_TEMPLATES[$tag], appends context. Returns combined text.

  3. gate_is_valid_tag(tag): returns 0 if tag exists in GATE_TEMPLATES, 1 otherwise.

  4. gate_check_playlist(): scans PLAYLIST_LINES for #TAG markers. Returns:
     * Total bead count and total gate count
     * Per-template counts
     * Gate density ratio
     * Violations against minimum rules

  5. gate_minimum_rules() — deterministic density requirements:
     * Every playlist with >1 bead MUST have at least 1 gate (zero = ERROR)
     * Density: at least 1 gate per GATE_DENSITY_RATIO beads (default 7, configurable). Low = WARNING.
     * #COMPLETENESS_SCAN: at least once per 10 beads or per epic. Missing = WARNING.
     * #SMOKE_TEST: at least once if playlist has >5 beads. Missing = WARNING.
     * #REVIEW: at least once per epic boundary. Missing = WARNING.

* Config in lib/config.sh:
  * GATE_DENSITY_RATIO=7 (configurable in .ralph/config — starting heuristic, tune after runs)
  * GATE_BUILD_CHECK="" (optional deterministic build command, informational only)
  * GATE_BUILD_EVERY=0 (run build check every N beads, 0 = disabled)

* Runtime parsing in lib/playlist.sh playlist_next():
  * After parsing @model, detect #TAG pattern.
  * Validate tag via gate_is_valid_tag(). If invalid: log error with line number and valid tags, return 1 (halts playlist).
  * If multiple #tags detected on same line: log error, return 1.
  * Store in globals: playlist_line_gate_tag, playlist_line_gate_context.

* In lib/loader.sh, add gates.sh to load order.

Acceptance criteria:
* GATE_TEMPLATES contains SMOKE_TEST, COMPLETENESS_SCAN, REVIEW
* gate_expand_tag() returns template + context at runtime
* Unknown tags are hard errors at parse time with helpful message
* Multiple tags per line are hard errors
* Tag-only lines (no context) expand to template text only
* #TAG is parsed in playlist_next() alongside @model
* Claude never sees raw #TAG — only expanded text
* Playlist file is never modified by expansion
* GATE_DENSITY_RATIO is configurable in .ralph/config
* gate_check_playlist() and gate_minimum_rules() report density analysis

title: Playlist Mode — Ordered Task Sequences with Prompt Injections
description:
Add --playlist FILE mode to ralph for executing an explicit sequence of bead tasks
interleaved with raw Claude prompts. This enables orchestrated multi-epic execution
with intermediate cleanup, review, and plan-adjustment steps.

MOTIVATION:
Ralph currently picks tasks reactively from br ready. For large planned work (e.g.,
39 tasks across 6 Flutter epics), we need:
1. Explicit execution order (not just dependency-graph order)
2. Intermediate non-bead prompts between tasks (review, fix, adjust beads)
3. Resumable execution (crash-safe via playlist line tracking)

PLAYLIST FORMAT:
Each line is one of:
* Bead ID (e.g., chippie-ogz3.1) — executed as normal bead task
* > Raw prompt text — executed as free-form Claude prompt (no bead)
* # Comment — skipped
* Blank line — skipped

DESIGN PRINCIPLES:
* Minimal changes to existing code (ralph is 1,430 lines — keep it simple)
* Playlist mode is an alternative to br-ready mode, not a replacement
* --playlist and --scope are mutually exclusive
* All existing features (circuit breaker, monitoring, tmux, remote) still work
* Playlist state (current line) persisted in .ralph_state for crash recovery

6 child tasks covering: config/args, playlist reader, raw prompt builder,
main loop integration, state tracking/resume, dry-run validation.
close_reason: All 8 child tasks implemented. Playlist mode adds --playlist FILE flag for ordered task execution with raw prompt injection lines, dry-run validation, state persistence/resume, monitor integration, completion reports, and auto-commit control.

4. ralph --playlist flutter.playlist --model sonnet → "Playlist complete" immediately

In the dry-run code path, either:

* Save state before dry-run starts and restore after, OR
* Skip playlist_line persistence when DRY_RUN=true

* Subsequent real run starts from line 0 (or wherever it was before dry-run)

title: Fix: local keyword used outside function in main loop
description:
BUG: ralph script line 57-58 uses `local` in the main while-loop body,
which is not inside a function. Bash only allows `local` inside functions.

CRASH: After completing bead tasks, when ralph hits the first > prompt line,
bash throws: "/Users/admin/dev/ralph/ralph: line 57: local: can only be used in a function"
This triggers the exit trap, ending the session prematurely.

LOCATION: ralph lines 57-58 (in the playlist else branch):
  local model_note=""
  local _saved_model=""

FIX: Replace `local` with plain variable assignments:
  model_note=""
  _saved_model=""

These are in the top-level while loop, not a function. Just drop the `local` keyword.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* ralph --playlist FILE processes > prompt lines without crashing
* Model override (@opus) still works correctly
close_reason: Fixed: removed local keyword from lines 57-58 in ralph main loop

title: Restore model override on invoke failure (break path)
description:
BUG: When invoke_claude fails (|| break) during a >@model prompt, the MODEL
variable stays overridden because the restore code on line 69 is skipped.

This means:
1. save_state persists model=opus instead of model=sonnet
2. Next run uses opus for ALL tasks (not just the review prompt)
3. The report shows wrong model

LOCATION: ralph lines 67-69
  invoke_claude         || break    # <-- break skips line 69
  # Restore model if overridden
  if [[ -n "$_saved_model" ]]; then MODEL="$_saved_model"; fi

FIX: Restore model BEFORE the break:
  invoke_claude || {
      if [[ -n "$_saved_model" ]]; then MODEL="$_saved_model"; fi
      break
  }

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* After a failed @opus prompt, MODEL is restored to the original value
* State file shows correct model after failure
close_reason: Fixed: model restored before break on invoke failure

title: Retry failed Claude invocations before stopping

* Log each retry: "Retry 2/3 for current task..."
* If all 3 fail, then break as current behavior
* Applies to both bead tasks and > prompt invocations
* Circuit breaker counts a failed-after-retries as no-progress (existing behavior)

LOCATION: ralph main loop, both bead and prompt paths where invoke_claude || break

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* Transient API error on attempt 1 succeeds on attempt 2 — no interruption
* 3 consecutive failures on same item — ralph stops with clear exit reason
* Retry count visible in logs and monitor
close_reason: VERIFY: Kill Claude mid-invocation (simulate failure), observe retry with augmented prompt containing exit code diagnosis + last output tail. After 3 failures, ralph stops with clear message. Raw logs saved to .ralph/logs/. NOTES: Restructured invoke_claude as retry wrapper around _invoke_claude_once. Added output capture via tee to .ralph/logs/, extract_failure_tail for log parsing, augment_prompt_with_failure_context for context-preserving retries, diagnose_exit_code for human-readable failure reasons.

title: Skip already-closed beads on playlist resume

When resuming a playlist (or after reset), ralph re-processes bead lines even
if the bead is already closed. It should skip them.

* Claude sees already-completed work, closes it again
* Wastes a full Claude invocation per already-closed bead

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR:
* Before claim_task, check bead status via br show
* If status is "closed", log "Skipping chippie-xxx (already closed)" and advance
* Count skipped beads in summary but not as "tasks completed"
* > prompt lines are never skipped (always re-run)

LOCATION: ralph main loop, playlist bead path, before claim_task

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* Reset + re-run playlist with 6 closed beads — all 6 skipped instantly
* Resume from crash — closed beads before playlist_line already skipped by position
* Logs clearly show which beads were skipped
* Skipped beads don't count toward total_tasks_completed
close_reason: VERIFY: Create playlist with mix of closed and open beads, run ralph --playlist FILE — closed beads logged as 'Skipping (already closed)' and not sent to Claude. NOTES: Added bead_already_closed() to tasks.sh, called before playlist_execute_bead in main loop.

title: Resume should retry in_progress beads skipped by crash
description:
BUG: When ralph is interrupted (Ctrl+C) during a bead task, the playlist_line
has already advanced past that bead. On restart, ralph picks up at the saved
playlist_line, skipping the unfinished bead entirely.

REPRO:
1. Ralph starts ogz3.8 (playlist_line advances to 42)
2. Claude invocation fails or user Ctrl+C's
3. State saved with playlist_line=42
4. Restart: ralph reads line 42, which is the review prompt — ogz3.8 is skipped
5. ogz3.8 stays in_progress forever

EXPECTED: On resume, before continuing from playlist_line, scan all prior
bead lines for any that are still in_progress. Retry those first.

ALTERNATIVE FIX: Don't advance playlist_line until the bead is closed or
released. Only advance on successful completion.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* Ctrl+C during bead task -> restart -> same bead retried
* Bead that was closed before crash -> not retried
* Bead left in_progress -> retried before continuing playlist
close_reason: Fixed: playlist_next no longer advances playlist_line. Uses _playlist_pending_line which only commits via playlist_advance() in save_state(). On failure, pending is cleared so final save_state doesn't advance.

description:
When a playlist finishes (all lines processed OR interrupted), ralph automatically
invokes Claude one final time to generate a structured markdown report.

BEHAVIOR:

* Creates .ralph/reports/ directory if it doesn't exist
* Invokes Claude with a report prompt that includes:
  - List of all playlist lines processed (bead IDs + prompt summaries)
  - For each bead: final status (closed/open/in_progress) via br show
  - Git log of all commits made during the session (git log --oneline since session_start)
  - Circuit breaker state and exit reason
  - Total tasks completed / total loops / runtime
* Claude writes report to .ralph/reports/<playlist-basename>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.md
* Report is committed: git add .ralph/reports/ && git commit

REPORT TEMPLATE (Claude fills in):
"""
# Ralph Playlist Report: <playlist name>
**Date:** <timestamp>  **Duration:** <elapsed>  **Model:** <model>

## Summary
- Tasks completed: X / Y
- Prompt injections run: A / B
- Exit reason: <reason>
- Circuit breaker: <state>

## Task Results
| # | Type | ID/Summary | Status | Commit |
|---|------|-----------|--------|--------|

## Commits
<git log --oneline>

## Issues Discovered
<any beads Claude opened/released during the run>

## Remaining Work
<beads still open from the playlist>

## Notes
<anything notable: blocked tasks, test failures, architectural decisions>
"""

title: Per-line model override — >@model syntax for prompt lines
description:
Allow playlist prompt lines to specify a model override with >@model syntax.

SYNTAX:
  > Run flutter analyze               — uses default --model
  >@opus Review all changes            — uses opus for this prompt only
  >@sonnet Fix codegen errors           — uses sonnet for this prompt only

PARSING (in playlist.sh playlist_next):
* After stripping >, check if next token starts with @
* If so, extract model name, set playlist_line_model to it
* Strip the @model prefix from playlist_current_line
* If no @model prefix, set playlist_line_model="" (use default)

INVOCATION (in ralph main loop, prompt branch):
* Before invoke_claude, if playlist_line_model is set:
  - Save current MODEL to _saved_model
  - Set MODEL=$playlist_line_model
* After invoke_claude:
  - Restore MODEL=$_saved_model

This should ONLY apply to > prompt lines, not bead lines.
Bead lines always use the --model flag value.

FILES TO MODIFY:
* lib/playlist.sh — playlist_next() parses @model prefix
* ralph — prompt branch saves/restores MODEL around invocation

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
* >@opus Review... uses opus model
* >@sonnet Fix... uses sonnet model
* > Plain prompt... uses default --model
* Bead lines unaffected
* Monitor/log shows which model is being used
* Dry-run shows model override in output
